question.problem:
In a music program at a college, an average of $45%$ of graduating students go on to pursue a career in music. Using the normal approximation to the binomial distribution, estimate the probability that in a graduating class of $200$ students, at least $110$ students will go on to pursue a career in music. Give your final answer to $3$ decimal places.

*Hint: The data below is taken from the table of values of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z)$ for the standard normal distribution. *

| $z$ | $\,0.05\,$ | $\,0.06\,$ | $\,0.07\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,2.6\,$ | $\,0.9960\,$ | $\,0.9961\,$ | $\,0.9962\,$ |
| $\,2.7\,$ | $\,0.9970\,$ | $\,0.9971\,$ | $\,0.9972\,$ |
| $\,2.8\,$ | $\,0.9978\,$ | $\,0.9979\,$ | $\,0.9979\,$ |
question.worked_solution:
Given a binomial random variable $X∼B(n,p),$ if 

- $np>5,$ and

- $n(1-p)>5,$

we can approximate $X$ as a normal random variable $Y$ with mean $\mu =np$ and variance ${\sigma }^{2}=np(1-p),$ that is, 

$$
Y∼N(np,np(1-p)).
$$

Here, we have $n=200$ and $p=0.45.$ Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}np & =200\cdot 0.45 \\  & =90 \\  & >5\,✓ \\ n(1-p) & =200\cdot (1-0.45) \\  & =110 \\  & >5.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

So, we can approximate our binomial random variable $X$ with a normal random variable $Y$ with mean

$$
\mu =np=(200)(0.45)=90
$$

and variance

$$
{\sigma }^{2}=np(1-p)=(200)(0.45)(1-0.45)=49.5.
$$

That is, we can approximate $X$ by $Y∼N(90,49.5).$

Now, we can estimate the desired probability $P(X\ge 110).$ Using a continuity correction, we have

$$
P(X\ge 110)≈P(Y>109.5).
$$

To compute this probability, we transform to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Y>109.5) & =1-P(Y\le 109.5) \\  & =1-P(Z\le \frac{109.5-90}{\sqrt{49.5}}) \\  & ≈1-P(Z\le 2.77) \\  & =1-Φ(2.77) \\  & =1-0.9972 \\  & =0.0028\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
P(X\ge 110)≈0.003.
$$

Note: Using a software package for the approximation gives a probability of $0.0028.$
